headline: OpenAI launches Grid Protectors and cites a large flexible-load agreement for its planned Georgia campus
summary: OpenAI announced Grid Protectors on 2 November 2026 as a program to arrange flexible power use at future compute campuses. It cites a Georgia Power agreement for a planned Effingham County campus expected to require about 3,200 MW, with up to 1,000 MW of demand response under a 25-year term. Georgia Power said its contract to serve OpenAI was approved through the Georgia PSC regulatory process. A joint PSC Staff/Georgia Power statement records staff review, compliance with prior orders and non-objection subject to stated terms; the PSC filing describes a 3,210 MW contract as deemed approved but does not identify its customer, and its public-summary ZIP was not inspectable. Georgia Power projects about $950 million in annual portfolio savings beginning in 2029 and at least $180 per year for a typical residential customer; these are future projections. The campus is not operating, and actual curtailment and customer outcomes remain unmeasured.
